cloze.s: The fire alarm went off at a truly ___ moment, right as the bride began her vows.

why: old cloze 'an ___ move' let foolhardy fit the meaning, and the article 'an' gave the answer away
coy (pretending to be shy, often flirting) and sheepish (embarrassed after a mistake) are not true synonyms
'interminable letter' could also fill the cloze
'anticipate' most often means 'expect', which misleads learners
'hopes to marginalize the market leader' could also fill the cloze
pretender (one who claims a throne) and impostor (one who pretends to be someone else) are not synonyms
harmony is too loose to count as a synonym
conversationalist means someone good at talking; speaker is not a synonym
bevy (a large group of things) is a near-synonym and could fill 'a ___ of dishes'
'assiduously follows the season, never missing a game' could also fill the cloze
gourmand often means a food lover, not someone who overeats
competitive is not the opposite of collegial

cloze.s: The two brothers ___ the fraud themselves, faking every signature without help from anyone.

why: inflict is not a synonym; old cloze repeated example 1 (same gang, same burglaries)
tedium is the quality of being boring, not the feeling
a boor is a rude person, not someone who does not value art
a prank is a trick played on someone, not an adventure
'fans in noisy exhilaration' could arguably fill the cloze
both could fill 'moved ___ through the dark house, avoiding every creaky floorboard'
'found the documentary truly encyclopedic; he learned more...' also fits the cloze
near-synonym (bad time vs bad sign); fits 'an ___ beginning'
'talking on his phone during the funeral was contemptible' also fits the cloze
'apologized meekly, accepting full blame' also fits the cloze
'He belatedly admitted that...' also fits the cloze
'Pundits who bicker on TV about every topic' also fits the cloze
could arguably fill "so ___ in college that his roommates rarely saw him without a textbook"
